rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2-2.5 and 3 - authors designed a solar-powered gravity-fed micro-tube irrigation system and field-tested it on a research farm plot, recording emitter discharges. Q2: Sections 3.1-3.4, Table 5, Fig. 5 - measured emitter discharge 0.801-1.034 L/h, overall emitter flow variation 18.96% (within ASAE 20% limit), CUC 93.65% (above ASAE 85% minimum), Du 91.55%; system judged to qualify on all criteria. Q4: Tables 3-4 and Section 4 - head losses computed per pipe section via Darcy-Weisbach/orifice equations; authors attribute low emitter flow variation to negligible head loss in mains and laterals with losses concentrated in micro-tubes. Q7: Sections 2.3 and 4 - laminar flow must be maintained in all pipe sections; water should be drawn from top 3/4 of pond depth and only after 72 h of runoff events to avoid clogging; design is specific to farm size and plot of ~200 m2. Q8: Sections 2.5 and 4-5 - acreage figures are indicative only and depend on crop and planting geometry; design specific to farm size; study carried out at a single location; qvar exceeded limit on laterals 7 and 9. Q9: Table 5 - CV of emitter discharge 5.40%, CD at 5% 0.16 L/h, and ranges across laterals for qvar, CUC (90.9-96.2%) and Du (88.3-94.6%).
rows.notes: The passage faithfully reports the study's own uniformity figures. However, the study measured hydraulic uniformity only; it did not measure water savings, crop water use, or water-use efficiency against any alternative, so the 'water_conservation' function is inferred from uniformity rather than demonstrated. The system is a gravity-fed micro-tube (star configuration) micro-irrigation system, a low-cost variant of drip, not a conventional dripper-based system; treated as within 'drip' here. Single plot (18 m x 11 m), single site, single evaluation method (emitter catch measurements). Q4 'yes' is based on design-stage head-loss calculations rather than measured pressure.

notes: Full text appears complete. Study is a system design and hydraulic performance evaluation (uniformity metrics, sediment content of pond water, cost); no agronomic or water-saving outcomes reported.
